To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) river corridor exchange space decreases systematically through a 5th-order river network, from the headwaters to the mainstem, (2) river corridor exchange time decreases systematically through a network, from the mainstem to the headwaters, and (3), river corridor exchange is not related to discharge or local geomorphic setting.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be careful when interpreting tracer test data and that we need to collect more data to improve our understanding of the controls on river corridor exchange.

the spatial and temporal variability of hyporheic exchange is much more complex than we have previously appreciated, and the development of a robust conceptual model will require more data collected at a greater number of sites and over a broader range of conditions.
